$comment: House writing style for every book Volume writes. Checkers in packages/core read this file; prompts receive bannedPhrases and rules as variables. Profiles and book templates may add to these lists but never remove the core rules without the owner's say.

rules.description: No em dashes anywhere in book text. Use a comma, colon, full stop or brackets.
No en dash used as a dash, and no en dash in number ranges: write 'pages 10 to 20'.
British spelling throughout (usToUkSpelling), with the context exceptions in spellingExceptions treated as warnings.
British phrasing (ukPhrasing): 'admitted to hospital', 'at university', 'A&E'. Warnings only, because context decides.
None of the bannedPhrases, plus any phrases banned in the author profile.
Non-fiction is written in the first person ('I', 'my', 'we') from the author profile, unless the book template or profile says otherwise. About the author stays third person (profile bio verbatim).
Contractions (I'm, don't, we've) are welcome in prose. They are not a style error.
Non-fiction narrative template: no bullet points, numbered lists or tables inside chapter prose. The optional Key Takeaways block after the prose is the only list allowed.
No tables in the narrative non-fiction or fiction templates.
Mix short and long sentences. Flag runs of five or more sentences of similar length, or three paragraphs opening the same way.
No 'firstly, secondly, thirdly' scaffolding or announced transitions ('moving on to...'). Let ideas lead into each other.
No sentence that simply restates the paragraph before it, and no one-line moral at the end of every section.
Explain any technical term the first time it appears, in plain words.
Do not reuse an example, story, metaphor or quote already listed in the book's used-already ledger.
Spell out one to nine in prose, figures for 10 and above, figures always with units and percentages ('5 mg', '12 per cent' or '12%' consistently within a book).
Never invent ISBNs, statistics, studies, quotes, testimonials, reviews, awards or sources. Matches of guardrailPatterns go to the claims report.
Do not open paragraphs with scaffolding such as 'Here's the', 'Here's how', 'Let's' or 'In this chapter, we will'. More than two in one section is flagged (aiHabits.paragraphOpeners).
Do not keep saying 'this is illustrative' or 'a composite'. The copyright page covers the stories; more than two such disclaimers in a book is flagged (aiHabits.illustrativeDisclaimers).
Define a term once, at first use, and give each piece of advice once. Repeated sentences, definitions and advice across sections are flagged by the repetition checker.

bannedPhraseMatching.dropFinalENote: Single words ending in e also match with the e dropped before -ing or -ed (ensure: ensuring, ensured).
bannedPhraseMatching.apostrophes: treat straight and curly apostrophes as the same
bannedPhraseMatching.note: Matches inside quoted source titles or proper names (for example a real organisation's name) are reported as warnings, not errors. Profiles can add phrases; they cannot remove these.

bannedPhrases: at the end of the day
moving on to the next topic
whether you are a beginner or an expert
whether you're a beginner or an expert

Book Architect Pro (AI tells): at the end of the day
moving on to the next topic
P02 BOK-10 stock phrases: whether you are a beginner or an expert
whether you're a beginner or an expert

spellingNote: Single words, lower case. The checker matches whole words case-insensitively and keeps the original capitalisation when it suggests a fix. Words in spellingExceptions depend on meaning, so the checker only warns. Quoted titles, names and URLs are never changed.
properNamesNote: Official proper names that keep their own spelling (often American). The spelling and phrasing checks skip them, case-sensitively. Add a name here, never a general word.
properNames: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Center for Disease Control and Prevention
National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health

spellingExceptions.program: Use 'programme' for a plan, TV or radio show or course; keep 'program' for computer software.
spellingExceptions.meter: Keep 'meter' for a measuring device (gas meter); use 'metre' for the unit.
spellingExceptions.check: Use 'cheque' only for a bank payment; 'check' is correct as a verb or noun meaning inspection.
spellingExceptions.tire: Use 'tyre' for a wheel; 'tire' is correct as a verb (to tire).
spellingExceptions.license: UK: 'licence' is the noun, 'license' is the verb.
spellingExceptions.practice: UK: 'practice' is the noun, 'practise' is the verb.
spellingExceptions.draft: Keep 'draft' for a document version or a bank draft; use 'draught' for air or beer.
spellingExceptions.dialog: Keep 'dialog' for a software dialog box; otherwise 'dialogue'.
spellingExceptions.curb: Use 'kerb' for the pavement edge; 'curb' is correct as a verb (to curb).
spellingExceptions.judgment: UK legal writing keeps 'judgment' for a court's decision; otherwise 'judgement'.
spellingExceptions.story: Use 'storey' for a floor of a building; 'story' for a tale.
spellingExceptions.inquiry: UK usage often prefers 'enquiry' for a general question and 'inquiry' for a formal investigation.

titleCase.rule: Capitalise the first letter of each word, as in the owner's drafts ('Fear, Pain, And Frustration As Drivers').
titleCase.hyphenated: Capitalise only the first part of a hyphenated word unless it is a proper noun ('The Art Of Verbal De-escalation').
titleCase.minorWordsNote: Set minorWordsMode to 'lowercase' in a profile or template to use standard title case (minor words lower case unless first or last).

guardrailPatterns.message: ISBN found. Only the ISBN the owner entered may appear.
guardrailPatterns.description: Any ISBN in text. Allowed only when it equals the owner-entered ISBN for this format.

guardrailPatterns.message: Number shaped like an ISBN-13.
guardrailPatterns.description: Bare 13-digit 978/979 numbers.

guardrailPatterns.message: Percentage claim. Needs a real source or removal.
guardrailPatterns.description: '40% of nurses...' style statistics.

guardrailPatterns.message: Percentage found. Check it has a real source.
guardrailPatterns.description: Any percentage in prose.

guardrailPatterns.message: Appeal to research. Name a real source from the research list or rewrite as opinion.
guardrailPatterns.description: 'Studies show', 'research suggests', 'experts agree'.

guardrailPatterns.message: Attributed claim. The source must be real and in the research sources.
guardrailPatterns.description: 'According to...' attributions. 'According to plan', 'according to your needs' and 'according to the instructions' are not attributed claims.

guardrailPatterns.message: Named or implied study finding. Verify or remove.
guardrailPatterns.description: 'A survey of 2,000 parents found...'. The word 'review' is not matched: 'when you review it you found' is not a study.

guardrailPatterns.message: Specific count of people. Needs a real source.
guardrailPatterns.description: Large specific counts presented as fact.

guardrailPatterns.message: Statistic in words (one in five, half of nurses). Needs a real source or removal.
guardrailPatterns.description: Ratios and shares written as words; percent-of only catches digits.

guardrailPatterns.message: Award or acclaim claim. Only if true and entered by the owner.
guardrailPatterns.description: Awards and acclaim. 'Won the argument', 'shortlisted for the job' and 'nominated for promotion' are not award claims; a prize word must follow.

guardrailPatterns.message: Bestseller or ranking claim. Remove unless verified by the owner.
guardrailPatterns.description: 'Bestselling author', '#1 bestseller', 'number one on Amazon'. Plain 'number one priority', 'Step #1' and 'no. 1' list numbers are not ranking claims.

guardrailPatterns.message: Quote attributed to a named person. Testimonials and real quotes must be supplied by the owner.
guardrailPatterns.description: A quotation followed by a named attribution.

guardrailPatterns.message: Review or rating claim. Never invented.
guardrailPatterns.description: Invented praise and ratings. The word testimonial is allowed when the sentence denies or advises about one (no testimonials, do not invent a testimonial, ask clients for a testimonial).

guardrailPatterns.message: URL in prose. Only links from the profile or the research sources are allowed, and only in back matter or resources.
guardrailPatterns.description: Real links in chapter text: a scheme (https://), www. or a domain with a path. Organisation names such as GOV.UK or NHS.uk are not links.

guardrailPatterns.message: Dose or clinical quantity. Clinical claim for the owner to verify.
guardrailPatterns.description: Medication doses and clinical quantities.

guardrailPatterns.message: Medical or clinical statement. Goes to the claims report.
guardrailPatterns.description: Medical and clinical language. 'Treat' only counts in a clinical context (treat symptoms, treated for), not 'treat it like'.

guardrailPatterns.message: Legal statement. Goes to the claims report.
guardrailPatterns.description: Legal claims and rights. 'sue' only counts as a verb for suing (not the name Sue).

guardrailPatterns.pattern: \b(?:completely safe|perfectly safe|safe for (?:everyone|children|babies)|risk[- ]free|no risk|harmless|cannot hurt|never dangerous)\b
guardrailPatterns.message: Safety claim. Goes to the claims report.
guardrailPatterns.description: Absolute safety claims.

guardrailPatterns.pattern: \b(?:(?<!\b(?:not(?!\s+only)|no|never|cannot|without|nor|neither|nothing|none|\w+n['’]t|rather\s+than|instead\s+of)\b(?:(?!\b(?:and|but|so|then|we|i|our)\b)[^.!?;:,\n]){0,40})guarantee[ds]?\b|proven to|100% (?:effective|safe|guaranteed)|will cure|works every time|the only book you need)
guardrailPatterns.message: Guarantee or promise of results. Remove or soften.
guardrailPatterns.description: Promises the book cannot prove. Negated uses (not a guarantee, no guarantee, never guaranteed, can't guarantee, do not offer guarantees, rather than a guarantee) are allowed.

guardrailPatterns.message: Em dash. Replace with a comma, colon, full stop or brackets.
guardrailPatterns.description: Em dash character.

guardrailPatterns.message: En dash. Use a comma or 'to'.
guardrailPatterns.description: En dash used as a dash or in a range.

aiHabits.$comment: Warnings (never errors) for habits the live AI writer overused. Openers are matched at the start of a paragraph, case-insensitive, after bold or italic markers; a section with more than maxPerSection of them gets a warning on each. Disclaimer markers are counted once per paragraph across the book (title page, copyright and contents excluded); more than maxPerBook gets a warning on each. Read by packages/core (checkText, checkBookStyle, checkDisclaimers) and the volume-house-style skill.

paragraphOpeners.message: Scaffolding opener "{match}" ({count} in this section, keep it to {max}). Start with the point itself.

illustrativeDisclaimers.message: "This is illustrative" style disclaimer ({count} in the book, keep it to {max}). One line on the copyright page covers every story.
